records.title: Retirement: Azure Stream Analytics PowerBI output connector
records.summary: Azure Stream Analytics jobs using the Power BI output connector stop on October 31, 2027; replace the connector before then.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Microsoft ends creation of Azure Stream Analytics jobs using the Power BI output connector on October 31, 2027, and stops existing jobs using it on that date. The change is specific to this connector.
what.financialConsiderations: The text above is from Microsoft’s announcement. Pricing and financial impact are workload-specific; review replacement-service pricing and your agreements before migrating.
what.html: Microsoft ends creation of Azure Stream Analytics jobs using the Power BI output connector on October 31, 2027, and stops existing jobs using it on that date. The change is specific to this connector.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: Plan to replace the Power BI output connector in each affected Azure Stream Analytics job before October 31, 2027. Microsoft recommends exploring Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric.
actions.guidance: Choose a reporting design that fits your workload, then test the selected Eventstream and Eventhouse path or another documented Stream Analytics output and Power BI DirectQuery combination before cutover. The migration article describes options but does not guarantee feature parity.

resources.title: Announcing the retirement of real-time streaming in Power BI
Simplifying Migration to Fabric Real-Time Intelligence for Power BI Real Time Reports

actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
Plan to replace the Power BI output connector in each affected Azure Stream Analytics job before October 31, 2027. Microsoft recommends exploring Real-Time Intelligence in Microsoft Fabric.

  1. Identify the reports and downstream consumers that use each affected job.
  2. Select a documented alternative that meets your processing and reporting requirements.
  3. Test event routing, queries, and reports before moving production workloads.

The migration article describes options but does not guarantee feature parity or provide a workload-specific migration plan.

impact.question: Where, and how much, am I impacted?
impact.introduction: Your affected environments, resources, and users.
impact.guidance: The retirement applies to Azure Stream Analytics jobs that use the Power BI output connector. The current product documentation says this connector is not available in Azure operated by 21Vianet or Azure Germany.
checklist: Inventory Azure Stream Analytics jobs that use the Power BI output connector.
Identify dependent Power BI reports, semantic models, applications, and owners.
Test the selected replacement path against each job's event flow and reporting requirements.

impact.html:

deadline.html:

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Azure stream analytics PowerBI output connector will be retired on Oct 31, 2027.

What is changing for Azure Stream Analytics Power BI output connector?
DateWhat happens
Beginning October 31st, 2024New customers will not be able to create new Azure Stream Analytics jobs with Power BI as output connector

Beginning Oct 31 31st, 2027Existing customers will not be able to create new Azure Stream Analytics jobs with Power BI as output connector

Beginning Oct 31 31st, 2027Existing Azure Stream Analytic jobs with Power BI output connector will be stopped

Reason for retirement: Power BI has announced retirement of real time streaming. Find out more details about Power BI Streaming Datasets retirement: real time streaming in Power BI.
We encourage you to transition to Fabric real time intelligence prior to the retirement date to experience the new capabilities of Fabric Real Time Intelligence including:
Eventstream
KQL Database
DataActivator
Real Time Dashboards
From now to 10/31/2027 existing customers can continue to use Azure stream analytics PowerBI output connector without disruption. On 10/31/2027 stream analytics jobs running with PowerBI output connector will be stopped. Resources to aid in your migration can be found below.
Required action
To avoid service disruptions, please follow these instructions to migrate to real time intelligence by 10/31/2027.
Learn more.

records.title: Retirement: Azure Health Data Services will be retired on October 31, 2025 in the Qatar Central region
records.summary: The announcement gives conflicting retirement dates for Azure Health Data Services in Qatar Central, so confirm the current service status and deadline before planning a migration.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: The Azure Updates item says Azure Health Data Services in Qatar Central will be retired because of resource consolidation and low regional usage. It directs customers to move workloads to another available region and warns that workloads and associated application data would be deleted. The same item includes both October 31, 2025 and October 31, 2024 as retirement dates. The current Microsoft Learn regional availability page lists Qatar Central for FHIR service and does not resolve whether this retirement proceeded.
what.financialConsiderations: The announcement gives no cost estimate. Compare the target region and service pricing for your workload, and confirm the current retirement status with Microsoft before committing to a migration.
what.html:
The Azure Updates item says Azure Health Data Services in Qatar Central will be retired because of resource consolidation and low regional usage. It directs customers to another available region and warns that workloads and associated application data would be deleted.

The same item includes both October 31, 2025 and October 31, 2024 as retirement dates. The current Microsoft Learn regional availability page lists Qatar Central for FHIR service but does not resolve whether this retirement proceeded.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: The announcement directs customers to move Qatar Central workloads to another available Azure Health Data Services region and preserve data they need; confirm the current service status and deadline with Microsoft before acting.
actions.guidance: Inventory Qatar Central workloads and data, confirm the applicable service and retirement status with Microsoft, and validate target-region availability before planning a migration. Preserve required data before any retirement or shutdown.
actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
Inventory Qatar Central workloads and data, confirm the applicable service and retirement status with Microsoft, and validate target-region availability before planning a migration.

Preserve required data before any retirement or shutdown; the announcement says workloads and associated application data would be deleted if the retirement applies.

impact.question: Where, and how much, am I impacted?
impact.introduction: Your affected environments, resources, and users.
impact.guidance: The announcement identifies Azure Health Data Services workloads in Qatar Central as affected. The current Learn regional list does not confirm whether the retirement proceeded, so compare your service and region with Microsoft's current status.
checklist: Identify Azure Health Data Services resources located in Qatar Central
Confirm which service and data are covered by the retirement notice
Record the status confirmation and any required migration or data-preservation work
impact.notice: This directory cannot inspect your Azure environment. The announcement dates conflict, and the current regional availability page does not establish whether the Qatar Central retirement proceeded.
impact.html:

  • Check associated data and applications that depend on those resources.
  • Confirm the retirement status and applicable date with Microsoft before relying on a migration window.

deadline.question: What is the deadline?
deadline.introduction: Key dates and the consequences of not acting.
deadline.dateGuidance: The announcement gives October 31, 2025 and October 31, 2024 as retirement dates. The current Learn regional availability page does not clarify which date applied or whether the retirement proceeded, so the deadline is unconfirmed.
deadline.consequences: If the retirement applies, the announcement says workloads and associated application data in Qatar Central would be deleted. Confirm current service status and preserve required data before acting.
deadline.html:
The deadline is unconfirmed: the announcement contains both October 31, 2025 and October 31, 2024, and current Learn regional information does not resolve the conflict.

If the retirement applies, workloads and associated application data in Qatar Central would be deleted. Confirm the current status with Microsoft and preserve required data.

records.title: Retirement: Change Analysis (classic) API in Azure Monitor is retiring
records.summary: Change Analysis (classic) was announced for retirement on October 31, 2025, and current Change Analysis uses Azure Resource Graph rather than the classic API.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: The preserved Azure Updates notice scheduled retirement of the Change Analysis (classic) API for October 31, 2025, and said classic workloads and associated application data would be deleted. Current Azure Monitor guidance describes Change Analysis powered by Azure Resource Graph but does not confirm whether any classic endpoint remains available.
what.financialConsiderations: The current Learn page says Azure Resource Graph Change Analysis is available at no extra cost. The reviewed sources do not state whether other query, storage, or migration costs apply to your architecture.
what.html:
The Azure Updates notice scheduled retirement of the Change Analysis (classic) API for October 31, 2025, and said classic workloads and associated application data would be deleted.

Current Change Analysis uses Azure Resource Graph. The Learn documentation describes that experience but does not confirm whether any classic endpoint remains available.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: The retirement notice directed customers to migrate to Change Analysis powered by Azure Resource Graph before October 31, 2025. That date has passed.
actions.guidance: The current experience uses POST Microsoft.ResourceGraph/resources for queries across tenants and subscriptions, or scoped Microsoft.Resources/Changes and Microsoft.Resources/Snapshots APIs. Check feature and resource-type coverage, replace classic calls, and test query results and alerts. Change history is queryable for 14 days; export results separately if you require longer retention.

resources.title: Analyze changes to your Azure resources with Change Analysis - Azure Resource Graph | Microsoft Learn

actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
The retirement notice directed customers to migrate to Change Analysis powered by Azure Resource Graph. The announced date has passed, so verify any remaining classic dependency instead of assuming it is still supported.

  • Review the current Azure Resource Graph Change Analysis APIs and supported resource types.
  • Replace classic calls and test query results, permissions, alerts, and downstream automation.
  • Plan separate exports when you need more than the documented 14-day change-history retention.

impact.question: Where, and how much, am I impacted?
impact.introduction: Your affected environments, resources, and users.
impact.guidance: The notice concerns the Change Analysis (classic) API. Current Change Analysis is based on Azure Resource Graph and covers control-plane changes; the Learn page says it does not observe data-plane changes or file and configuration changes over App Service.
checklist: Search application code, scripts, SDK usage, and automation for calls to the classic Change Analysis API.
Identify dependent alerts, reports, and operational workflows.
Compare required resource types and query history with the current Azure Resource Graph experience.
impact.notice: No tenant access. This directory cannot determine whether your applications still call the classic API or whether your resources are affected. Verify callers and current service status in your own environment.
impact.html:
The announced scope is the Change Analysis (classic) API. The current Azure Resource Graph experience covers control-plane changes, but the Learn page says it does not observe data-plane changes or file and configuration changes over App Service.

  • Search code, scripts, SDK use, and automation for classic API calls.
  • Identify dependent alerts, reports, and operational workflows.
  • Check required resource types and history retention against the new experience.

deadline.question: What is the deadline?
deadline.introduction: Key dates and the consequences of not acting.
deadline.dateGuidance: The preserved Azure Updates notice gives October 31, 2025 as the exact date. It has passed; current Learn documentation describes Azure Resource Graph Change Analysis but does not confirm the classic API's post-retirement availability.
deadline.consequences: The notice said classic workloads and associated application data would be deleted. Because current documentation does not confirm whether legacy endpoints still operate, verify any remaining dependency directly rather than relying on continued availability.
deadline.html:
The retirement has passed. Current Learn documentation does not confirm the classic API's post-retirement availability.

The notice said classic workloads and associated application data would be deleted. Verify any remaining dependency directly rather than relying on continued availability.

records.title: Retirement: Support for TLS 1.0/1.1 in Application Insights Availability Tests will be retired
records.summary: Application Insights availability-test web-test execution stopped supporting TLS 1.0 and 1.1 and the listed legacy TLS 1.2 and 1.3 cipher suites and curves; affected tests can fail and stop ingesting data.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Application Insights Availability Tests no longer support TLS 1.0 and 1.1 or the listed legacy TLS 1.2 and 1.3 cipher suites and elliptical curves. The change applies to availability-test web-test execution, not availability-test resource-management operations.
what.financialConsiderations: The announcement does not quantify financial impact. Review the cost of any endpoint changes or replacement monitoring against your workload and agreements.
what.html:
Application Insights Availability Tests no longer support TLS 1.0 and 1.1 or the listed legacy TLS 1.2 and 1.3 cipher suites and elliptical curves.

The change affects web-test execution, not availability-test resource-management operations.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: Ensure each remote endpoint used by an availability test, including dependent requests, supports at least one TLS version, cipher suite, and curve combination supported by the test service.
actions.guidance: Inventory test targets and dependent requests, then have each endpoint owner verify support for a documented combination. Update endpoints that lack one, and validate the tests afterward. Microsoft Learn says the negotiated TLS configuration can't be viewed directly in test results; use the TLS troubleshooting details when investigating failures.

resources.title: Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn
Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn
Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn
Application Insights availability tests - Azure Monitor | Microsoft Learn

actions.supportGuidance: For a specific environment, contact the team that owns the remote endpoint or use Azure support.
actions.html:
Ensure every endpoint contacted by an availability test, including dependent requests, supports at least one combination documented for the test service.

  1. Inventory test targets and dependent requests.
  2. Ask endpoint owners to verify supported TLS versions, cipher suites, and curves.
  3. Update incompatible endpoints and validate test results.

The negotiated configuration isn't displayed directly; use TLS troubleshooting details when investigating failures.

impact.question: Where, and how much, am I impacted?
impact.introduction: Your affected environments, resources, and users.
impact.guidance: The change affects Application Insights availability-test web-test execution. Microsoft Learn says affected resources can stop ingesting data and some features can stop working; resource-management operations are outside this deprecation.
checklist: Inventory Application Insights availability tests and their remote endpoints.
Include dependent requests and identify the owners of each endpoint.
Compare endpoint support with the published TLS combinations and review test failures.
impact.notice: This directory cannot inspect your tenant or determine which tests are affected. A test's negotiated TLS configuration cannot be viewed directly, so verify endpoint support with its owner.
impact.html:
Only availability-test execution is in scope. An affected Application Insights resource can stop ingesting data and some features can stop working; resource-management operations are not covered by this change.

  • Inventory each test and its remote endpoints.
  • Include dependent requests and identify endpoint owners.
  • Compare endpoint support with the published TLS combinations and review test failures.

deadline.question: What is the deadline?
deadline.introduction: Key dates and the consequences of not acting.
deadline.dateGuidance: The stated deadline has passed. Microsoft Learn gives May 1, 2025 as the date the legacy configurations stopped being supported for availability-test execution.
deadline.consequences: Affected Application Insights resources can stop ingesting data and lose access to required application components, causing some features to stop working. Tests whose endpoints share a supported TLS combination are not described as affected.
deadline.html: The deadline has passed. Affected resources can stop ingesting data and lose access to required application components, causing some features to stop working.

progress.question: How can I track progress?
progress.introduction: What work remains, and what needs attention.
progress.guidance: Review test results for TLS-related failures and use the TLS Transport troubleshooting details. The negotiated TLS configuration itself isn't exposed, so confirm endpoint support with its owner.
checklist: Record each test, remote endpoint, dependent request, and owner.
Confirm supported TLS combinations with each endpoint owner.
Review test results and TLS troubleshooting details after endpoint changes.
progress.storageNote: This page does not store progress. Track owners, migration decisions, and verification results in your team's own system.

tracking.guidance: Review availability-test results and the TLS Transport troubleshooting details for TLS failures; the negotiated TLS configuration can't be viewed directly, so verify each endpoint's supported combinations with its owner.

progress.html:
Use a team-owned plan to coordinate endpoint verification; the catalog does not inspect tests or track migrations.

  • Record each test, endpoint, dependent request, and owner.
  • Review test results and TLS Transport troubleshooting details for TLS failures.
  • The negotiated TLS configuration is not exposed; confirm each endpoint's supported TLS versions, cipher suites, and curves with its owner.

records.title: Retirement: Azure AI Image Analysis 4.0 Preview APIs retiring on March 31, 2025
records.summary: The Image Analysis 4.0 preview API versions and some preview-only operations retired on March 31, 2025; the GA service has a separate scheduled retirement on September 25, 2028.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: The Image Analysis 4.0 preview API versions listed in the announcement retired on March 31, 2025. Product Recognition, background removal, and other preview-only capabilities have separate retirement details; the general Image Analysis 4.0 service is now scheduled to retire on September 25, 2028.
what.financialConsiderations: The text above is from Microsoft’s announcement. Pricing and financial impact are workload-specific; review replacement-service pricing and your agreements before migrating.
what.html:
The Image Analysis 4.0 preview API versions listed in the announcement retired on March 31, 2025. Calls to those versions no longer work.

The preview-only retirement also covered Product Recognition and background removal; current documentation identifies Custom Image Classification and Custom Object Detection preview APIs among the retired features. The general Image Analysis 4.0 service is a separate lifecycle item and is scheduled to retire on September 25, 2028.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: If a workload still references a listed preview version or retired preview feature, replace that dependency rather than relying on it. The original notice recommended Data Plane API 2024-02-01 for supported Image Analysis use; current Learn guidance says to plan migration from the overall Image Analysis API and lists alternatives by scenario. The migration guide has a September 25, 2026 planning target and a September 25, 2028 transition deadline, so verify the current timeline before scheduling.
actions.guidance: Inventory API versions and preview-only features, map each use case to a supported alternative, test it in staging, then update and validate production workflows. The current migration guide recommends Document Intelligence for OCR and Read scenarios and the Face API for face scenarios; other options depend on the use case.

Migrate from Azure Vision in Foundry Tools - Image Analysis

actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.

  • The current migration guide recommends Document Intelligence for OCR and Read scenarios and the Face API for face scenarios.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
On March 31, 2025, the Image Analysis 4.0 Preview APIs will be retired. Before that date, you’ll need to migrate your Azure Image Analysis workloads to the Image Analysis 4.0 GA API.

We encourage you to make the transition sooner to gain access to improvements such as multimodal embedding, synchronous OCR, people detection, image tagging, smart cropping, caption, dense caption, and image object detection.

These preview Image Analysis 4.0 APIs will retire on March 31, 2025:

2022-07-31-preview

2022-10-12-preview

2023-02-01-preview

2023-04-01-preview

2023-07-01-preview

v4.0-preview.1

These features will no longer be available with the retirement of the preview API versions:

Model customization

Background removal

Product recognition.

Required action

To avoid service disruption, update your workloads to use the newer GA API version: Data Plane 2024-02-01.

After March 31, 2025, API calls to the older versions won't work. For more information, please refer to the Image Analysis documentation.

Help and support

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support request.

Microsoft announced that Fabric Runtime 1.1 would be retired and disabled in March 2025. Its announcement recommended Runtime 1.3 at that time.

Current Fabric documentation lists Runtime 1.3 as end-of-support announced and Runtime 2.0 as the latest generally available runtime. The original recommendation should not be treated as current guidance.

actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.

records.title: Retirement: Azure Automation will discontinue execution of PowerShell runbooks using AzureRM modules from February 1, 2025
records.summary: Azure Automation stopped executing PowerShell runbooks that use AzureRM modules on February 1, 2025; migrate and test them with Az PowerShell.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: Azure Automation's February 1, 2025 cutoff stopped execution of runbooks that use AzureRM modules; the AzureRM PowerShell module itself had been unsupported since February 29, 2024.
what.announcement: Azure Automation stopped executing PowerShell runbooks that use AzureRM modules on February 1, 2025. The AzureRM PowerShell module itself had been unsupported since February 29, 2024.
what.financialConsiderations: The announcement and migration guidance do not quantify a financial impact.
what.html: Azure Automation stopped executing runbooks that use AzureRM modules on February 1, 2025. The AzureRM PowerShell module itself had been unsupported since February 29, 2024.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Find AzureRM dependencies, update the scripts and modules, then validate each runbook before deploying the change.
actions.guidance: The cutoff has passed, so identify affected runbooks and replace AzureRM dependencies with Az PowerShell. Search scripts for AzureRM cmdlets and inspect installed modules; update cmdlet names, modules, parameters, and any changed return-value assumptions because AzureRM scripts do not automatically work with Az. Use the migration toolkit to prepare and review script changes, test the updated runbooks in your environment, then deploy them and remove AzureRM modules from the Automation account.

resources.title: Migrate Azure PowerShell scripts from AzureRM to Az

actions.supportGuidance: Use the AzureRM-to-Az migration guide and toolkit for script conversion and breaking-change checks.
actions.html:
The February 1, 2025 cutoff has passed. Find runbooks that use AzureRM modules, update the scripts and dependencies to Az PowerShell, test them, and remove AzureRM modules from the Automation account.

  1. Inventory runbooks and search scripts for AzureRM cmdlets and modules.
  2. Use the migration toolkit to review proposed edits, then update cmdlet names, modules, parameters, and changed return-value assumptions.
  3. Test each updated runbook in your environment, deploy the validated version, and remove the retired AzureRM modules.

impact.introduction: The change applies to Azure Automation PowerShell runbooks that use AzureRM modules; the announcement does not quantify separate financial effects.
impact.guidance: Runbooks that still depend on AzureRM cannot execute under the retired workflow. AzureRM is no longer maintained or supported. Az PowerShell is the migration path, but existing scripts can require changes beyond cmdlet renaming because modules, parameters, and return values may differ.
checklist: Identify Automation runbooks that import or call AzureRM modules.
Check scripts for AzureRM cmdlets, modules, parameters, and return-value assumptions.

Confirm the runbook executes with the AzureRM modules removed.

Runbooks that still depend on AzureRM cannot execute under the retired workflow. AzureRM is no longer maintained or supported, and Az PowerShell scripts can require changes to modules, parameters, and return values.

  • Identify runbooks that import or call AzureRM modules.
  • Check cmdlets, parameters, and return-value assumptions during migration.
  • Test each replacement and confirm it runs after AzureRM modules are removed.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Starting February 1, 2025, Azure Automation will discontinue execution of all runbooks that use AzureRM modules.
The AzureRM PowerShell module has retired on February 29, 2024, in favour of Az PowerShell that offers more security, stability and functionalities. You must update all runbooks from AzureRM to Az PowerShell and remove AzureRM modules from your Automation account, to ensure continued support and updates.

Refer to migration resources for guidance on transitioning from AzureRM to Az PowerShell module.

records.title: Retirement: Resources interacting with Azure Automation using TLS 1.0/1.1 protocol will be blocked from March 1, 2025
records.summary: Azure Automation blocks connections using TLS 1.0 or 1.1, affecting webhooks, Hybrid Runbook Workers, DSC nodes, and certain managed machines.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Azure Automation blocks connections using TLS 1.0 or 1.1 from webhooks, agent-based and extension-based User Hybrid Runbook Workers, DSC nodes, and machines managed by Azure Automation Update management or Change Tracking. Hybrid Worker jobs using those protocols fail.
what.financialConsiderations: Costs depend on the changes needed in your environment.
what.html:
Azure Automation blocks connections using TLS 1.0 or 1.1 from webhooks, agent-based and extension-based User Hybrid Runbook Workers, DSC nodes, and machines managed by Azure Automation Update management or Change Tracking.

Hybrid Worker jobs using those protocols fail.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: Configure affected clients to use TLS 1.2 or higher.
actions.guidance: Identify affected clients and configure their operating systems, libraries, and webhook callers to negotiate TLS 1.2 or higher. Check the platform-specific guidance and test the connection and jobs after the change.
actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
Configure affected clients to use TLS 1.2 or higher.

  1. Identify webhook callers, Hybrid Workers, DSC nodes, and affected managed machines.
  2. Review the platform-specific guidance and update the applicable TLS configuration.
  3. Test connections and Hybrid Worker jobs after the change.

Avoid unnecessarily restricting clients to TLS 1.2 only, because that can prevent negotiation of newer protocols.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.0 and 1.1 are security protocols for establishing encryption channels over computer networks. Starting March 1, 2025, your resources interacting with Azure Automation using TLS 1.0/1.1 protocols won’t be able to connect to Azure Automation. All interactions through Webhooks, Agent-based/Extension-based User Hybrid Runbook Workers, Automation DSC navigating on the outdated TLS protocols will be blocked. All jobs running or scheduled on Hybrid Workers using TLS 1.0 and 1.1 protocols will fail.

Ensure your resources interact with Azure Automation using TLS 1.2 or higher. Follow these steps to disable TLS 1.0/1.1 protocols and enable TLS 1.2 or higher for Windows and Linux machines.

records.title: Retirement: All Azure Automation jobs running on Agent-based Hybrid Worker will be stopped from 1 April 2025
records.summary: Azure Automation agent-based User Hybrid Runbook Workers for Windows and Linux retired on August 31, 2024, and jobs on them were scheduled to stop on April 1, 2025; extension-based workers are the supported replacement.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: The agent-based (V1) User Hybrid Runbook Worker for Windows and Linux, which depends on the Log Analytics agent, retired on August 31, 2024 and is no longer supported. The extension-based (V2) Hybrid Runbook Worker, installed through the Hybrid Runbook Worker VM extension, is the supported platform. All jobs running on agent-based Hybrid Workers were scheduled to stop starting April 1, 2025.
what.financialConsiderations: The text above is from Microsoft’s announcement. Pricing and financial impact are workload-specific; review replacement-service pricing and your agreements before migrating.
what.html:
The agent-based (V1) User Hybrid Runbook Worker for Windows and Linux, which depends on the Log Analytics agent, retired on August 31, 2024 and is no longer supported.

The extension-based (V2) Hybrid Runbook Worker, installed through the Hybrid Runbook Worker VM extension, is the supported platform. All jobs running on agent-based Hybrid Workers were scheduled to stop starting April 1, 2025.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.guidance: Move each agent-based worker to an extension-based worker. In the Azure portal, open the Hybrid worker groups of the Automation account, select the group, choose Hybrid Workers and then Add, and select the existing agent-based machine. The Platform column shows Agent based (V1) or Extension based (V2). Before you start, confirm that the machine has a system-assigned managed identity (it is enabled when you add the worker if it is absent), that non-Azure machines are Azure Arc-enabled, and that the operating system is supported. A machine can run both worker types at the same time, and installing the extension does not affect the agent-based worker. Documented limits for extension-based workers: Python 3.11 or later is not supported on the Linux worker, Virtual Machine Scale Sets are not supported, and Windows PowerShell 5.1 is required (PowerShell Core is not supported). Because the stop date has passed, any remaining agent-based worker is unsupported.

resources.title: extension-based User Hybrid Runbook Worker (Windows & Linux)
Deploy an extension-based Windows or Linux User Hybrid Runbook Worker in Azure Automation

actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
Move each agent-based worker to an extension-based worker.

  1. In the Azure portal, open the Hybrid worker groups of the Automation account and select the group.
  2. Choose Hybrid Workers, then Add, and select the existing agent-based machine.
  3. Check the Platform column, which shows Agent based (V1) or Extension based (V2).

Before you start, confirm that the machine has a system-assigned managed identity (it is enabled when you add the worker if it is absent), that non-Azure machines are Azure Arc-enabled, and that the operating system is supported. A machine can run both worker types at the same time, and installing the extension does not affect the agent-based worker.

Documented limits for extension-based workers:

  • Python 3.11 or later is not supported on the Linux worker.
  • Virtual Machine Scale Sets are not supported.
  • Windows PowerShell 5.1 is required, and PowerShell Core is not supported.

Because the stop date has passed, any remaining agent-based worker is unsupported.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Starting April 1, 2025, all jobs running on agent-based User Hybrid Runbook Worker will be stopped.

Azure Automation Agent-based User Hybrid Worker (Windows & Linux) retired on August 31, 2024, and is no longer supported. It poses a potential Security risk since Agent-based Hybrid Worker has not been getting any Security fixes post-retirement. Hence, it is strongly recommended that you move to extension-based User Hybrid Runbook Worker (Windows & Linux) for executing Hybrid jobs.

Key benefits of new approach:
- Enhanced security posture for your VMs through access control using system-assigned managed identities, instead of self-managed certificates
- Improved operational productivity for keeping the workers up to date, using automatic upgrades and at-scale management of the VMs
- Simplified installation of extension while eliminating the need to install Log Analytics agent.

Follow the instructions to migrate your agent-based User Hybrid Runbook Workers to extension-based Hybrid Workers before April 1, 2025.

records.summary: Since March 31, 2025, Azure HDInsight cluster connections require TLS 1.2 or later; clients limited to TLS 1.0 or 1.1 cannot connect.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Beginning March 31, 2025, Azure HDInsight cluster connectivity is available only through TLS 1.2 or later. This notice applies to HDInsight clusters, not other Azure TLS retirements. The current HDInsight guidance says public HTTPS endpoints accept TLS 1.2 by default and lets you set the gateway minimum to 1.2.
what.financialConsiderations: The announcement specifies no separate pricing change. Assess any costs associated with updating clients or cluster configurations in your environment.
what.html:
Beginning March 31, 2025, Azure HDInsight cluster connectivity is available only through TLS 1.2 or later. This notice applies to HDInsight clusters, not other Azure TLS retirements.

HDInsight public HTTPS endpoints accept TLS 1.2 by default. You can set the gateway minimum to TLS 1.2 when creating a cluster.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: If any application or client still depends on TLS 1.0 or 1.1, update it to use TLS 1.2 or later and verify connectivity. The announcement also recommended upgrading HDInsight clusters to version 5.1 by March 31, 2025; that date has passed.
actions.guidance: Inventory HDInsight clusters and connecting applications, then test TLS 1.2 or later from each client. The HDInsight gateway minimum can be set during cluster creation with the minSupportedTlsVersion property.

resources.title: Transport layer security in Azure HDInsight

actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
Update clients that depend on TLS 1.0 or 1.1 to use TLS 1.2 or later, then verify connectivity.

The announcement also recommended upgrading clusters to HDInsight 5.1 by March 31, 2025; that date has passed. HDInsight documents the minSupportedTlsVersion property for setting the gateway minimum during cluster creation.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Customers that have Azure HDInsight cluster is using TLS version 1.1 or lower are requested to upgrade to clusters have TLS version 1.2.
To enhance security and provide best-in-class encryption for your data, we'll require all connections to Azure HDInsight clusters to be secured using Transport Layer Security (TLS) 1.2 or later beginning March 31, 2025, when connectivity will only be available through TLS 1.2 or later versions. This retirement notice applies only to Azure HDInsight clusters; all other TLS retirements aren’t impacted by this announcement.

Your clusters maybe configured to use TLS 1.1 or lower due to outdated clusters, or other applications connected to Azure HDInsight clusters that only support lower TLS versions.

Required action

Upgrade to versions 5.1 of the Azure HDInsight cluster with TLS version 1.2 by March 31 to keep your clusters working as expected. To avoid potential service disruptions, confirm that your resources that interact with Azure services are using TLS 1.2 or later.

If they're already exclusively using TLS 1.2 or later, you don't need to take further action.

If they still have a dependency on TLS 1.0 or 1.1, transition them to TLS 1.2 or later.

If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support request .

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Azure Data Studio (ADS) will be officially retired on February 28, 2026, to streamline development efforts and improve the user experience in Visual Studio Code (VS Code). VS Code will become the recommended cross-platform tool for developers building backend databases.
ADS will be supported until February 28, 2026, to ensure users have sufficient time to transition. Any files or database projects available locally in ADS will remain accessible through February 28, 2026.
Database projects created in ADS can be opened and continued in VS Code without any migration steps. Most extensions in ADS are also available in VS Code, though some SQL-based exceptions exist. In those cases, customers should consider SQL Server Management Studio 21 (SSMS 21) as an alternative to VS Code.
Learn more.

However, the Microsoft Software Installer (msi) for this agent is still publicly available for download. If you have a legacy script that downloads this msi, then this script may fail when the product is retired.

Status Monitor v1 is being retired because it was replaced by Application Insights Agent (formerly named Status Monitor v2) in 2019. Customers seeking auto-instrumentation for .NET workloads on-premises servers should use Application Insights Agent.

Recommended Action
If you have used this product in the past, ensure that you remove any code that downloads the ApplicationInsightsAgent.msi installer.

References
Retired msi urls:
http://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/?LinkID=522371
https://appinsightsstatusmonitor.blob.core.windows.net/version91/ApplicationInsightsAgent.msi

More Information
If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Azure Monitor - Microsoft Q&A.

Bing Search APIs, with your LLM is retired on March 6th 2025. Any existing instances of Bing Search APIs, with your LLM will be decommissioned completely, and the product will no longer be available for usage or new customer signups.

Note that this retirement will apply to partners who are using the S15, S16, S17, or S18 resource.

We recommend transitioning to Grounding with Bing Search as part of Azure AI Agents.

Grounding with Bing Search allows your Azure AI Agents to incorporate real-time public web data when generating responses with an LLM.

Help and support
If you have questions, contact support by creating a support ticket.
Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

records.title: Retirement: GPU image (Preview) in AKS
records.summary: AKS retired the GPU Image (preview) on January 10, 2025; new node pools using it are blocked, existing pools are unsupported and cannot be updated to add a GPU size, and current GPU guidance requires supported sizes and drivers.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: AKS retired the GPU Image (preview) on January 10, 2025. New node-pool creations using that image are blocked, and existing node pools that use it are unsupported. The official announcement directs customers to migrate GPU VHD-enabled node pools to GPU-enabled pools made with supported alternatives.
what.financialConsiderations: The official announcement does not quantify price, downtime, or workload-specific cost effects. Check the costs and availability of the supported GPU VM SKU you select before migration.
what.html:
AKS retired the GPU Image (preview) on January 10, 2025. New node-pool creations using the image are blocked, and existing node pools using it are unsupported.

The announcement directs customers to move GPU VHD-enabled workloads to node pools made with supported alternatives.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: The January 10, 2025 retirement date has passed. Identify node pools using the retired GPU Image (preview) and migrate affected workloads to supported GPU-enabled node pools. The announcement lists two alternatives: use a supported GPU VM SKU and manually install the NVIDIA device plugin, or use a supported GPU VM SKU, skip automatic driver installation, and install the NVIDIA GPU Operator. Validate the selected approach before moving production workloads.
actions.guidance: Current AKS GPU guidance describes managed and self-managed GPU node pools, supported VM-size and driver prerequisites, and notes that an existing pool cannot be updated to add a GPU size. Account for this restriction when planning a supported replacement pool. The guide does not verify the retired preview image or its retirement date.

On January 10, 2025, the AKS GPU Image (preview) retired. New node pool creations with the GPU image (preview) are now blocked. Existing node pools using the GPU Image (preview) are now unsupported. Follow the detailed steps in our documentation create GPU-enabled node pools using the alternative supported options on AKS.

Required Action
Migrate your existing AKS workloads from GPU VHD-enabled node pools to GPU-enabled node pools created using the supported alternative solutions.
Alternative solutions include:
Create a node pool with a supported GPU VM sku and manually install the NVIDIA device plugin.
Create a node pool with a supported GPU VM sku, skip automatic driver installation, and manually install the NVIDA GPU Operator.

Help and Support
If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support request.

records.title: WebAssembly System Interface (WASI) Node Pools in AKS
records.summary: AKS no longer supports preview WASI node pools, and new pools cannot be created after May 5, 2025; no shutdown date for existing pools is stated.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: AKS ended support for preview WebAssembly System Interface (WASI) node pools, and new WASI node pools can no longer be created after May 5, 2025. The announcement recommends SpinKube for running WebAssembly workloads but does not give a shutdown date for existing pools.
what.financialConsiderations: The announcement does not quantify migration cost or replacement-service pricing. Assess the cost and operational requirements of your AKS and SpinKube design before changing workloads.
what.html:
AKS ended support for preview WebAssembly System Interface (WASI) node pools, and new pools can no longer be created after the announced cutoff.

The announcement recommends SpinKube for WebAssembly workloads but does not give a shutdown date for existing WASI pools.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: The announcement recommends creating node pools using the AKS-supported SpinKube alternative and migrating existing workloads.
actions.guidance: SpinKube is not documented as an automatic conversion of a WASI node pool. Review the deployment prerequisites and limitations, create and validate the replacement on AKS, move workloads in a controlled rollout, and remove old resources only after validation. The Learn guide requires Linux nodes and current versions of Azure CLI, kubectl, Helm, and Spin.

resources.title: Create WebAssembly System Interface (WASI) node pools in Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) to run your WebAssembly (Wasm) workload (preview)
Deploy SpinKube to Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) to run serverless WebAssembly (Wasm) workloads

actions.supportGuidance: For environment-specific help, use Azure support; Microsoft Q&A is a community support channel.
actions.html:
Plan a workload migration to SpinKube rather than assuming an existing WASI pool can be converted automatically.

  1. Review the SpinKube requirements and confirm the AKS cluster meets them.
  2. Deploy and test SpinKube on AKS.
  3. Move and validate workloads before removing old resources.

The Learn guide documents prerequisites and deployment steps, not a direct WASI-to-SpinKube conversion.

records.title: Retirement: Canonical Ubuntu 20.04 LTS Reaching End of Standard Support on May 31, 2025
records.summary: Standard support for Canonical Ubuntu 20.04 LTS ended on May 31, 2025; existing virtual machines can continue running without standard Canonical updates.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Standard support for Canonical Ubuntu 20.04 LTS has ended. Existing virtual machines can continue running, but Canonical no longer provides standard security, feature, and maintenance updates. You can migrate to a supported Ubuntu LTS release or use Ubuntu Pro for expanded security maintenance; Ubuntu Pro coverage varies by repository and package.
what.financialConsiderations: The reviewed Microsoft sources do not compare Ubuntu Pro pricing with migration costs. Confirm the applicable licensing and support terms before choosing a path.
what.html:
Standard support for Canonical Ubuntu 20.04 LTS has ended. Existing virtual machines can continue running, but Canonical no longer provides standard security, feature, and maintenance updates.

You can move workloads to a supported Ubuntu LTS release or use Ubuntu Pro for expanded security maintenance. Ubuntu Pro coverage differs by repository and package.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: Review Ubuntu 20.04 LTS virtual machines and choose either a tested upgrade to a supported LTS release or Ubuntu Pro for continued security maintenance.
actions.guidance: Microsoft says there is no direct upgrade from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS to 24.04 LTS: upgrade first to 22.04 LTS and then to 24.04 LTS, or deploy a fresh 24.04 LTS instance and migrate the workload. Scope and test the process with your applications. Ubuntu Pro can be enabled on supported existing Ubuntu Server VMs without redeployment.

resources.title: Canonical Ubuntu 20.04 LTS Reaching End of Standard Support
Canonical Ubuntu LTS end of standard support guidance

actions.supportGuidance: For Azure VM platform issues, use Azure Support. Canonical provides Ubuntu Pro support options for eligible plans.
actions.html:
Choose and test a supported operating-system path for each workload. Microsoft documents an upgrade from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS to 22.04 LTS and then to 24.04 LTS; there is no direct upgrade path to 24.04 LTS. A fresh 24.04 LTS deployment is another option.

Alternatively, evaluate Ubuntu Pro for expanded security maintenance. Confirm package coverage and subscription terms before choosing.

  1. Inventory Ubuntu 20.04 LTS VMs and application dependencies.
  2. Choose an upgrade or redeployment path and test it outside production.
  3. Validate the operating system, applications, and security updates before completing rollout.

Check which repositories and workloads require continued security maintenance.

  • Identify application dependencies, owners, and support requirements.
  • Check package coverage and decide whether to upgrade or use Ubuntu Pro.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
We’re announcing the upcoming end of standard support for Ubuntu 20.04 LTS on May 31, 2025, as we focus on delivering a more secure and optimized Linux experience. You can continue using your existing virtual machines, but after this date, security feature, and maintenance updates will no longer be provided by Canonical, which may impact system security and reliability

Recommended action
Take action before May 31, 2025, to stay on a supported operating system. Microsoft recommends migrating to the next Ubuntu LTS release or upgrading to Ubuntu Pro for extended security and maintenance from Canonical.

Upgrading to Ubuntu 22.04 LTS or Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
While there’s no direct upgrade path from Ubuntu 20.04 LTS to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, you can directly upgrade to Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, and then to Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, or directly install Ubuntu 24.04 LTS.

Please refer to the Ubuntu Server upgrade guide for detailed, step-by-step instructions.

Ubuntu Pro – Extended Security Maintenance to 2030
New virtual machines can be deployed with Ubuntu Pro from the Azure Marketplace. You can also upgrade existing virtual machines to Ubuntu Pro by purchasing directly from Canonical.
Learn more:
Read the blog.
Refer to the documentation

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Azure Intelligent Recommendations service will be retired on March 31, 2026.

This service is being retired due to changes in strategy and focus with the onset of the Copilot era. We encourage you to identify alternative options.

From now to March 31, 2026 existing customers can continue to use Intelligent Recommendations without disruption. New customer deployments will stop immediately.

On March 31, 2026 – workloads running Intelligent Recommendations, as well as the Intelligent Recommendations Machine Learning models, will be deleted. Resources to aid in your off-boarding can be found below.

Required action
Identify alternatives or build your own alternative.
Migrate all your traffic to your chosen alternative.
Stop calling Recommendations endpoint before the shutdown date.
Delete all service endpoints, all modeling, and all Intelligent Recommendations accounts you have in the Azure portal before the shutdown date.

To view impacted resources in the Azure portal, you can navigate to the Intelligent Recommendations accounts page here: Intelligent Recommendations Accounts - Microsoft Azure.

More Information
If you have questions, please contact us at irhelp@microsoft.com. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, create a support request.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Azure Synapse Analytics Data Explorer (Preview) was scheduled to retire on October 7, 2025. Microsoft said workloads running on it would be deleted and associated application data lost after that date, and recommended migration to Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric.
what.financialConsiderations: The text above is from Microsoft’s announcement. Pricing and financial impact are workload-specific; review replacement-service pricing and your agreements before migrating.
what.html:
Azure Synapse Analytics Data Explorer (Preview) was scheduled to retire on October 7, 2025. Microsoft said that after this date workloads running on Synapse Data Explorer would be deleted and associated application data lost.

The announced date has passed. Microsoft recommended Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric as the successor, but the documented migration capability is still labeled preview.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: If a source cluster is still available, first verify its status and eligibility; the documented migration to Fabric Eventhouse is a preview and is irreversible.
actions.guidance: The migration guide requires a running source cluster, a Fabric-enabled target workspace, and Owner and Admin roles on the source and target. Validate the cluster, migrate it, monitor the operation, and verify the Eventhouse and databases. Not all connections, policies, security settings, or export operations migrate automatically.
actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
If a Synapse Data Explorer source cluster is still available, verify its current status and eligibility before attempting a migration. The documented migration creates an Eventhouse and is irreversible; the feature is in preview.

  1. Confirm the source cluster is running, remove resource locks, and verify target capacity and required roles.
  2. Validate the cluster, then migrate the entire cluster and its databases using the documented Fabric REST API.
  3. Plan for migration limitations: some data connections, policies, security settings, and export operations require separate handling or are unsupported.
  4. Verify the Eventhouse and migrated databases, then update clients to the Eventhouse endpoints.

The migration can interrupt new ingestion, and the retired service date has passed. Do not assume a cluster remains available or that deleted data can be recovered.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Synapse Data Explorer (Preview) will be retired on October 7, 2025. The next generation of Synapse Data Explorer offering is evolving to become Eventhouse in Real-Time Intelligence, part of Microsoft Fabric.
Eventhouse offers the same powerful features and capabilities of Synapse Data Explorer, but with enhanced scalability, performance, and security. ​

Key Dates:

March 31, 2025: Last day of public preview. After this date, you can continue using Synapse Data Explorer without any disruption in your existing subscriptions. You will also be able to create new Data Explorer pools within your existing subscriptions. However, creating Data Explorer pools in new subscriptions will no longer be possible.

October 7, 2025: Retirement day of Synapse Data Explorer. After this date, workloads running on Synapse Data Explorer will be deleted, and the associated application data will be lost.

Required action ​

We encourage you to transition to Eventhouse in Microsoft Fabric, by October 7, 2025. By making the switch, you'll gain access to the new capabilities of Fabric, including end-to-end analytics in a unified SaaS platform and access to open data formats in OneLake.
Learn more.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
You’re receiving this notification because you're associated with one or more Azure subscriptions that use Azure SQL Database using FSV2 offer.

In 2020, we launched FSV2-series as a hardware choice Azure SQL Database, and we’ve been monitoring customer adoption and feedback on this hardware option. Due to limited regional availability of this hardware, we’ll be retiring support for the FSV2-series hardware option for Azure SQL Database on October 1, 2026.

How does this affect me?

Starting On October 1, 2025, customers who haven’t already deployed Azure SQL Database on FSV2-series won’t be able to create new databases on FSV2-series.

Existing Azure SQL Database FSV2-series customers can continue to use the databases until October 1, 2026 but should plan to migrate out of the FSV2-series HW on to other options within Azure SQL Database before then.

After October 1, 2026, Azure SQL Databases running on FSV2-series HW will no longer be supported. Remaining databases running on FSV2-series HW will be migrated to General-purpose tier with similar configurations.

Required action

We recommend transitioning to the Hyperscale premium-series or General-purpose standard-series (Gen5) service tier before October 1, 2026 to maintain comparable performance levels.

Learn more:
For more information on SQL Database service tiers, see azure documentation here.
FAQ for FSV2 offer retirement

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Beginning March 31, 2028, the Azure App Service custom backup feature will no longer back up linked databases configured as part of the Azure App Service custom backup feature. We strongly recommend that you use the native backup and restore tools available with the respective databases, instead.

Before March 31, 2028, the App Service team will remove the ability to include linked databases as part of new custom backup configurations for App Service web applications. The schedule for this change is as follows:
November 2025 for linked MySQL and PostgreSQL databases
April 2026 for linked Azure SQL and SQL Server databases

App Service web applications with existing custom backups that already include linked databases will continue to back up the linked databases until retirement of the App Service custom backup linked database feature on March 31, 2028.

Recommended action
To avoid data or functionality loss, implement backup strategies for databases linked to your App Service web applications by 31 March 2028. For further information, please refer to the guidance available here.

More Information
If you have questions, get answers from community experts in Microsoft Q&A.

Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

records.title: Retirement: Docker Compose Feature for Azure App Service to Be Retired on March 31, 2027 – Replaced by Sidecars in Azure App Service
records.summary: Azure App Service Docker Compose retires on March 31, 2027; migrate multi-container apps to sidecars and validate compatibility before cutover.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: The Azure Updates announcement says the Docker Compose feature for multi-container Azure App Service applications will be retired on March 31, 2027. It says supported Compose applications may experience HTTP 5xx errors after that date unless migrated to sidecar containers. The announcement describes sidecars as providing separate container management and integration with App Service features.
what.financialConsiderations: The announcement gives no migration cost estimate. Review the App Service and any supporting resource charges for your chosen configuration before migration.
what.html:
The Docker Compose feature for multi-container Azure App Service applications is scheduled to retire on March 31, 2027. The announcement warns that Compose applications may experience HTTP 5xx errors after that date unless migrated to sidecar containers.

It describes sidecars as providing separate container management and integration with App Service features.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: Migrate Docker Compose applications to App Service sidecar containers before March 31, 2027, then validate the migrated application before cutover.
actions.guidance: Microsoft's migration guide recommends script-based migration for simple configurations and also documents a manual path. Back up the app, check prerequisites and feature limitations, create a deployment slot, migrate containers, validate the slot, and only then swap it into production. Sidecars do not support every Compose behavior, including startup ordering, Compose networks, secrets, and persistent Azure storage in the documented scenarios.
actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
Microsoft's migration guide recommends script-based migration for simple configurations and also documents a manual path.

  1. Back up the app and check the documented prerequisites and sidecar limitations.
  2. Create a deployment slot and map each Compose service to a sidecar container.
  3. Restart and validate the migrated app in the slot.
  4. Swap the slot into production only after validation.

The guide lists unsupported or changed behaviors, including Compose startup ordering, networks, secrets, and persistent Azure storage in the documented scenarios.

impact.question: Where, and how much, am I impacted?
impact.introduction: Your affected environments, resources, and users.
impact.guidance: The announcement applies to multi-container applications using Docker Compose on Azure App Service. It warns of possible HTTP 5xx errors after retirement if applications have not migrated.
checklist: Identify Azure App Service apps configured with Docker Compose
Check each app's containers, ports, storage, networking, secrets, and startup dependencies
Test sidecar behavior in a deployment slot before production cutover
impact.notice: The migration guide documents sidecar compatibility limits, including shared localhost networking and unsupported Compose features. Validate your own configuration; this directory cannot inspect your apps.
impact.html:
The affected scope is Azure App Service applications using Docker Compose for multi-container deployments. The announcement warns of possible HTTP 5xx errors after March 31, 2027 if they have not migrated.

  • Inventory Compose apps and their container dependencies.
  • Check storage, networking, port, secret, and startup-order requirements against sidecar limitations.
  • Validate each migrated application before production cutover.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
The docker compose feature will be retired on March 31, 2027, please transition to the sidecar container by that date. The sidecar containers allow you to create multi-container applications with a more intuitive configuration and integration with all other features of Azure App Service.

We encourage you to transition to sidecar containers prior to the retirement date. Sidecar provides several benefits over docker compose, including:
An easier configuration system to deploy and manage your multi-container applications.
Full Azure portal integration allows you to manage each container separately, check the status and logs.
Seamless integration with Azure App service features like VNet and Managed Identity.

Please note that your docker compose web applications will be supported through March 31, 2027. After March 31, 2027, your docker compose applications will start facing disruptions resulting in HTTP 5xx errors unless they have been migrated to sidecar containers.
Learn more.

records.title: Retirement: Kubenet Networking for Azure Kubernetes Service to Be Retired on March 31, 2028
records.summary: Kubenet networking for Azure Kubernetes Service is scheduled for retirement on March 31, 2028, with Azure CNI Overlay as the supported migration target.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Kubenet networking for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is scheduled to retire on March 31, 2028. The official migration guidance describes a forward-only migration from Kubenet to Azure CNI Overlay; Azure CNI Powered by Cilium is a separate data-plane update.
what.financialConsiderations: The reviewed sources do not estimate the cost impact for your clusters. Compare the supported networking options and any changed infrastructure or network requirements against your own workload and pricing.
what.html:
Kubenet networking for Azure Kubernetes Service is scheduled to retire on March 31, 2028. The migration guidance describes a forward-only move to Azure CNI Overlay; Azure CNI Powered by Cilium is a separate data-plane update.

Costs and network requirements depend on the cluster and chosen configuration.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Required actions, options, and available support.
actions.recommendedAction: Migrate affected Kubenet clusters to Azure CNI Overlay before March 31, 2028.
actions.guidance: The Learn guide supports a direct Kubenet-to-Overlay update. Check prerequisites first: Kubernetes 1.27 or later, no dynamic IP allocation, no enabled network policy, and no Windows node pool using Docker. The migration is irreversible and reimages all node pools simultaneously. Review route-table cleanup and use a user-assigned managed identity when a Kubenet route table must be detached.

resources.title: upgrade to Azure Container Networking Interface (CNI) overlay

actions.supportGuidance: For help with your specific environment, contact your Microsoft account team or Azure support.
actions.html:
Migrate affected clusters to Azure CNI Overlay before March 31, 2028. The supported migration is forward-only and cannot be reversed.

  • Confirm Kubernetes 1.27 or later, no dynamic IP allocation, no enabled network policy, and no Windows node pool using Docker.
  • Review route-table cleanup; detaching the Kubenet route table requires a user-assigned managed identity.
  • Plan for simultaneous node-pool reimaging and test the change before production.

impact.question: Where, and how much, am I impacted?
impact.introduction: Your affected environments, resources, and users.
impact.guidance: Only AKS clusters using Kubenet are in scope. The Learn guide identifies possible network disruption during simultaneous node-pool reimaging and cautions that overlay pod IPs are not reachable from outside the cluster nodes.
checklist: Find AKS clusters using Kubenet across subscriptions and environments.
Check route tables, pod CIDRs, network policies, node operating systems, and Kubernetes versions.
Test application connectivity and policy behavior after an overlay migration.
impact.notice: No tenant access. This directory cannot identify your AKS networking mode or assess cluster readiness. Confirm scope and prerequisites in your subscriptions.
impact.html:
Only AKS clusters using Kubenet are in scope. The update reimages node pools simultaneously and can disrupt networking; overlay pod IPs are not reachable from outside the cluster nodes.

  • Find Kubenet clusters across subscriptions and environments.
  • Check route tables, pod CIDRs, policies, operating systems, and Kubernetes versions.
  • Test application connectivity and network policies before production migration.

On March 31, 2028, kubenet networking for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) will be retired.

To avoid service disruptions, you'll need to follow these instructions to upgrade to Azure Container Networking Interface (CNI) overlay before that date, when workloads running on kubenet for AKS will no longer be supported.

records.summary: Azure Container Registry retires Docker Content Trust (DCT) on March 31, 2028; Learn gives May 31, 2026 for when new or previously unenabled registries cannot enable DCT, while the announcement gives September 30, 2025, and disabling DCT permanently deletes trust data and signatures but not images.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The change and what it means, including technical and financial considerations.
what.announcement: Azure Container Registry (ACR) is retiring Docker Content Trust (DCT) on March 31, 2028. Microsoft Learn confirms the removal date and describes disabling DCT and adopting Notation. For new or previously unenabled registries, Learn says DCT cannot be enabled starting May 31, 2026; the preserved Azure Updates announcement gives September 30, 2025. These dates conflict and the available sources do not resolve the discrepancy. Disabling DCT permanently deletes trust data and signatures, but not container images.
what.financialConsiderations: The announcement does not quantify price, service charges, downtime, or workload-specific financial effects. Review costs and requirements for your chosen replacement before migration.
what.html:
Azure Container Registry is retiring Docker Content Trust (DCT). Microsoft Learn describes disabling DCT and adopting Notation. Disabling DCT permanently deletes DCT trust data and signatures, but not container images.

For new or previously unenabled registries, Learn gives May 31, 2026 as the restriction date; the preserved announcement gives September 30, 2025. The sources do not resolve this conflict.

For new or previously unenabled registries, Learn gives May 31, 2026 as the restriction date, while the preserved announcement gives September 30, 2025; confirm applicability with Microsoft.
actions.guidance: Microsoft Learn describes disabling DCT and adopting Notation. Inventory registries, signing and verification workflows, and dependent policies before making the change. Disabling DCT permanently deletes trust data and signatures but not images. The Learn restriction date differs from the preserved announcement; confirm current applicability with Microsoft.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
Azure Container Registry (ACR) implements Docker Content Trust (DCT), allowing image publishers to sign their images and image consumers to verify that the images they pull are signed. With advancements in technology, Docker Content Trust no longer meets the requirements of modern supply chain security for containers. As a result, Docker Content Trust will be deprecated and no longer available in ACR after March 31, 2028. If you currently use Docker Content Trust, you should transition to the Notary Project ecosystem, including their open-source supply chain tool, Notation.

How does this affect me?
Starting September 30, 2025, customers will no longer be able to enable Docker Content Trust on Azure Container Registry.
Data stored in Azure Container Registry for signing and verifying signatures with Docker Content Trust will be permanently deleted on March 31, 2028.
Docker Content Trust function will be completely removed from Azure Container Registry on March 31, 2028.

Required Action
Start your transition to Notary Project today and enhance the security and trust of your container ecosystem. Use the following articles to get started.

what.question: What is changing?

what.announcement: Manually registered Azure VPN Clients used for point-to-site (P2S) connections with Microsoft Entra ID authentication are being retired. Manually registered Azure VPN Clients for point-to-site connections using Microsoft Entra ID authentication are being retired. New connections with a manually registered client can no longer be created.

The current Learn migration guide gives different retirement dates for Azure Public Cloud and certain sovereign clouds.

sourceReview.originalAnnouncement:
You’re receiving this notice because your access control role is associated with subscriptions that use a manually registered Azure VPN client for point-to-site VPN connections.

On March 31, 2028, we’ll be retiring manually registered Azure VPN clients for point-to-site connections with Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

To improve security, we’ll only be supporting Microsoft-registered VPN clients after that date. Beginning 30 December 2025, it will no longer be possible to create point-to-site connections with a manually registered client.

Recommended action

To prevent disruptions, migrate manually registered Azure VPN clients to a Microsoft-registered VPN client for point-to-site connections with Microsoft Entra ID authentication before 31 March 2028.

More Information

If you have general questions, ask community experts in Microsoft Q&A. If you have a support plan and you need technical help, open the Azure portal and select the question mark icon at the top of the page.

Learn more about service retirements that may impact your resources in the Azure Retirement Workbook. Please note that retirements may not be visible in the workbook for up to two weeks after being announced.

D, Ds, Dv2, Dsv2, and Ls series Azure Virtual Machines will retire on May 1st, 2028. These VMs will no longer be able to be used or purchased after this date. To ensure any applications and workloads running on these VMs will be operating in the future, you need to migrate your D, Ds, Dv2, Dsv2, and Ls series VMs workloads to a newer VM generation
Three-year reserved instances for these VMs can also no longer be purchased or renewed starting on May 1, 2025. One-year reserved VM instances for these VMs will not be available for purchase or renewal starting July 1, 2026 (previously May 1, 2027 – learn more here).
If you have a three-year reserved instance contract for these VMs, you’ll still receive your reservation benefit for the remainder of the contract. To plan for this change and avoid unexpected billing, we recommend reviewing your current reservation orders to identify impacted VMs and their expiration dates.
For pricing details please refer to the VM pricing pages. For additional support, you can create a support request by following this process here. Ubuntu 18.04 on Azure Kubernetes Service will be retired on June 17, 2025. Please transition to a supported Ubuntu version by that date.

records.title: Retirement: Ubuntu 20.04 Node Pools in AKS
records.summary: AKS will stop supporting Ubuntu 20.04 node pools on March 17, 2027, remove their node images, and prevent scaling; current guidance recommends Kubernetes 1.35 or later for migration.

what.question: What is changing?
what.introduction: The retirement applies to Azure Kubernetes Service node pools using Ubuntu 20.04; it does not retire AKS or other Ubuntu node images.
what.announcement: AKS will stop supporting Ubuntu 20.04 node pools on March 17, 2027. Current migration guidance recommends Kubernetes 1.35 or later and requires separate validation for FIPS and confidential VM node pools.

what.html:
The retirement applies to Azure Kubernetes Service node pools using Ubuntu 20.04. It does not retire AKS or other Ubuntu node images.

The announcement originally described Kubernetes 1.33 or 1.34 targets for confidential VM and FIPS workloads. Current AKS documentation now recommends Kubernetes 1.35 or later for migrating Ubuntu 20.04 node pools.

actions.question: What do I need to do?
actions.introduction: Identify Ubuntu 20.04 node pools and move them to a supported OS and Kubernetes combination before the retirement.
actions.recommendedAction: Inventory Ubuntu 20.04 node pools, choose a currently supported OS and Kubernetes version compatible with required features, then test and upgrade them before March 17, 2027.
actions.guidance: Current AKS node image guidance says to migrate Ubuntu 20.04 node pools by upgrading to Kubernetes 1.35 or later. Check your cluster’s available upgrade path, quota, node pool OS SKU, and required features before choosing a target. For confidential VM pools, current guidance makes Ubuntu 24.04 the default for the Ubuntu OS SKU on Kubernetes 1.35 through 1.38; Ubuntu 22.04 is not supported with confidential VMs. FIPS cannot be combined with confidential VMs, and the current FIPS table lists Ubuntu 20.04 and 22.04, but not 24.04, as supported Ubuntu versions. Test the selected combination and workload before rollout.

Ubuntu 20.04 on Azure Kubernetes Service will be retired on March 17, 2027. Please transition to a supported Ubuntu version by that date.

Ubuntu 20.04 has been replaced by newer supported versions, including Ubuntu 22.04 and Ubuntu 24.04. We encourage you to transition to Ubuntu 22.04+ before the retirement date.

To avoid service disruptions, scaling restrictions, and remain supported, please follow our instructions to upgrade your Kubernetes version to 1.34+ by March 17, 2027. For more information on this retirement, see AKS GitHub.
